title: Why Japanese People NEVER Tip
description: You tip your waiter 20% and feel generous. In Japan? That same tip is an INSULT. Here's the wild reason why.

sections.narration: You just had the BEST sushi of your entire life. In Tokyo. It was unreal.
sections.visual_notes: Boy sitting at sushi bar, eyes wide, plate of colorful sushi in front of him, chopsticks in hand, sparkles around food

sections.narration: So you slap a big tip on the table. Twenty bucks. You feel like a HERO.
sections.visual_notes: Boy placing money bills on the table with a proud grin, thumbs up, money fanned out

sections.narration: And the waiter RUNS after you. Down the street. Waving your money.
sections.visual_notes: Waiter in apron sprinting down a street, arm stretched out holding money, boy turning around looking confused

sections.narration: Not because you overpaid. Because you just disrespected him. To his FACE.
sections.visual_notes: Close-up of waiter looking serious with arms crossed, money on the ground between them, boy looking shocked with sweat drops

sections.narration: See in Japan, amazing service isn't a bonus. It's the MINIMUM. It's called omotenashi.
sections.visual_notes: Waiter bowing perfectly with a tray balanced on one hand, Japanese text showing omotenashi, sparkle effects around him

sections.narration: Every waiter, every taxi driver, every convenience store worker — they give you EVERYTHING. Every time. No exceptions.
sections.visual_notes: Three panels: taxi driver opening door, convenience store worker wrapping a package with a bow, waiter pouring tea with perfect posture

sections.narration: So when you tip? You're basically saying — wow, I didn't think you'd actually be GOOD at your job.
sections.visual_notes: Boy holding out money with a naive smile, waiter with a giant question mark above head looking confused and a little hurt

sections.narration: That's like handing a doctor five bucks and going — thanks for not killing me!
sections.visual_notes: Boy handing a coin to a doctor in white coat, doctor staring at the coin with a deadpan expression, speech bubble with exclamation mark

sections.narration: But HERE'S the part that broke my brain.
sections.visual_notes: Boy's head literally cracking open like an egg, brain visible, explosion lines around head, dramatic zoom

sections.narration: Japanese workers don't earn LESS because there's no tipping. They earn a LIVING WAGE. The menu price already covers fair pay.
sections.visual_notes: Japanese menu with price circled showing equals sign to happy waiter with full wallet, green checkmark above

sections.narration: Meanwhile in America? Servers make TWO DOLLARS an hour. And pray that you're feeling generous.
sections.visual_notes: American waiter looking sad holding two tiny coins, empty tip jar next to him, rain cloud above his head

sections.narration: So which system is actually broken? Japan figured this out CENTURIES ago. Your grandma's rules — finally explained.
sections.visual_notes: Split screen: left side Japan flag with happy waiter and thumbs up, right side question marks and confused face, CuriousAsian logo at bottom
